notes: The supplied 'a' of 'a blind beggar' was moved from the adjective to the noun: rule 58 puts a determiner supplied for an anarthrous adjective-plus-expressed-noun phrase on the noun and warns in terms against reading it off English word order because it stands next to the adjective. The verse already read ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ → 'a great multitude' that way, so the accepted alignment was inconsistent with itself under rule 24.
The first καί of the genitive-absolute string is aligned to 'with', the ASV's rendering of the coordination; leaving it unrepresented and folding 'with' elsewhere is the competing reading.
